title: Characteristics of headache after craniotomy for resection of supratentorial meningiomas or low-grade gliomas and after elective clipping of unruptured intracranial aneurysms
summary: Headache is common after brain surgery, but its causes are not well understood. It may result from injury to nerves and tissue during surgery, or surgery may trigger a headache disorder such as migraine or tension-type headache. In this study, we interview patients who undergo surgery for a benign or low-grade brain tumour, or in whom an unruptured bulge of a brain artery (aneurysm) is closed with a clip. Interviews take place before surgery, 7–14 days after surgery, and after 3 and 12 months, in person or by telephone. In addition, we analyse data from routine care (surgery, anaesthesia, imaging). No additional examinations or treatments are performed. The aim is to describe headache after surgery more precisely and to identify factors that influence its occurrence and course.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients scheduled for craniotomy and resection of a supratentorial
meningioma or glioma (2)
- Patients who have undergone elective clipping of an unruptured saccular
intracranial aneurysm
- Age ≥ 18
Exclusion criteria:
Other secondary headaches (e.g., following sinus vein thrombosis, hypotension,
meningitis, empyema, subdural hematoma)
- Recurrent, multiple, or irradiated meningiomas/gliomas
- Ruptured (subarachnoid hemorrhage), previously treated, or non-saccular (e.g.,
fusiform, dissecting) aneurysms
- Extensive, diffusely infiltrating meningiomas
- Lack of written consent or lack of capacity to consent
